surfaces.part: left cut side wall (brown strip, x about 0-3)

answer.evidence: The ramp is one uniformly speckled earth plane filling rows 0-47. It has no front-edge line, eave shadow or south-facing vertical face. Only a slightly darker inset border (rows 0-46) suggests the slope. The two narrow vertical strips at left and right are the cut-through side walls, ending in a dark base line at row 47, with grass at their tops (rows 0-1). Below row 48 the same texture continues as flat ground. The whole piece reads as a flat walkable surface seen from above, not a standing volume with a top and a front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 8 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. Its near-flat coverage is 0%, the same as both references, so there are no flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline carries a tint. By eye the edges are dark brown, set against orange-brown rail posts and tan earth, which reads as a dark material tone rather than a black sticker line. The ramp surface is built from horizontal tan and brown bands with step edges. The soil strip at the bottom has grain and speckle, and the top edge picks up a small green lip. It is not as dense as the best grass clumps, but it reads clearly as packed earth and is at least as rich as the paving reference. Texture is only moderate: the banding is somewhat regular and the individual tones are less varied than the references' grain. Overall it is acceptable beside the references and does not look thinner or flatter.
